extracted.intended_audience: educated readers, statesmen, and policymakers interested in constitutional design and the French Revolution (British public/political class)
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and critique principles and practical requirements for structuring a durable republican constitution, with attention to representation, executive authority, local government, currency, and social habits. The page offers prescriptive norms and warnings drawn from historical precedent and practical effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to moral and political realities (study human nature)
rubrics_metrics.description: A constitution must make explicit reference to moral and political matters—the concerns, actions, passions, and interests of men—rather than relying solely on abstract metaphysics, geometry, or arithmetic ('Hominem non sapiunt').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designers must study human nature, habits, and the effects of civil life; avoid purely abstract, mechanical schemes that ignore moral and social realities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of citizens according to real differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Good legislators classify citizens according to birth, education, profession, periods of life, residence, modes of acquiring property, and the quality of property, treating them as different 'species' requiring different roles and privileges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate appropriate situations, privileges, and protections to different classes so each can perform functions suited to their habits and capacities; this classification helps secure balance and permanence in a republic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide methodical subordination and disciplined institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: A durable constitution requires methodical subordination, settlement, and institutions that inculcate discipline (e.g., military or other methodical elements) so that parts of the state are coherently ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lay foundations of settlement and disciplined subordination early rather than relying only on abstract equality; avoid creating bodies that lack internal discipline or habitual connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reducing citizens to a homogeneous mass
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not 'confound all sorts of citizens ... into one homogeneous mass' or reduce people to 'loose counters' used only for arithmetic counts of representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect real distinctions among citizens; failure to do so undermines capacity to provide appropriate roles, protections, and checks in governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct connection and accountability between representative and constituents
rubrics_metrics.description: Representatives must be chosen in a way that preserves a real connection to, and accountability toward, those they represent; excessive intermediary election layers make deputies ambassadors of states rather than representatives of people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid multi-stage election circuits that sever responsibility; ensure electors can know candidates' fitness and retain some hold upon them by obligation or dependence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize intervening electoral gradations that prevent accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple successive elections and magistracies intervening between primary electors and the ultimate representative render responsibility impossible and make representatives effectively unaccountable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design elections so that the directness of choice and the ability to hold representatives to account remain intact; avoid rules (e.g., multi-year ineligibility after service) that frustrate learning and continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a standing, fundamental government as centre of unity
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be a standing, independent government — a 'government of reference' — that originates and points representation and secures a territory as a coherent whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representation should be subordinate to a stable authority that embodies unity, rather than making the elective assembly the sole sovereign with no independent reference point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a senate or stabilizing council
rubrics_metrics.description: A republican government requires some body analogous to a senate — a middle, steadying council between the popular assembly and the executive — to give continuity, consistency, and a point of reference for foreign states and citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an institutional check and stabilizing influence; don't compose a state solely of one active legislative assembly and an executive lacking independent counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give the executive deliberative discretion (not a merely degraded or mechanical king)
rubrics_metrics.description: The executive should not be merely a passive channel or an instrument without deliberative discretion; reducing the executive to a machine is perilous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design an executive with genuine functional competence and some independent authority to act and advise; avoid making the office purely ceremonial or entirely controlled by the assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain territorial coherence; avoid severing into many independent republics
rubrics_metrics.description: The scheme that breaks the country into many small, nearly independent republics tends to sever ties and render the nation incoherent, lacking constitutional means of connection, coherence, or subordination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve bonds of union, provincial attachments, and institutions that connect subordinate divisions to a central authority; do not atomize the polity into disconnected units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve local knowledge and habitual civil institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Local magistrates, revenue collectors, bishops, and curates must be acquainted with their districts and parishes; disrupting these habitual relations undermines effective governance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reorganizations that leave officials strangers to their districts; keep local governance grounded in local habit and experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not destroy ancient social bonds (religion, polity, laws, manners)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conqueror-like destruction of existing institutions and manners severs ties that combine and rally people in distress; wholesale eradication weakens social coherence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reform with respect for historical institutions and cultural bonds; avoid policies that deliberately annihilate preexisting social structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using confiscation and compulsory paper currency as the primary cement of the state
rubrics_metrics.description: Relying on confiscation paired with forced paper currency may temporarily bind republics together but is unstable: if currency fails, the 'cement' disappears and increases dissociation and confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finance policy must be prudent and based on stable foundations; avoid making political unity depend on coercive fiscal instruments liable to collapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent an oligarchy formed by managers of paper circulation and state sales
rubrics_metrics.description: Unbacked paper money and the power to turn confiscated land into marketable assets concentrates influence in the hands of managers and speculators, creating an ignoble oligarchy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guard against concentrating monetary and land-direction powers; ensure currency is grounded and limit opportunities for speculative appropriation of public assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid turning the national economy into general gambling/speculation
rubrics_metrics.description: A polity that makes speculation and changes in currency value pervasive forces all citizens into gambling-like exposure, destroying industry, economy, and prudent provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve a stable medium of exchange and economic predictability so labor, saving, and investment make sense; do not institutionalize speculation as civic policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure representation emanates from a government existing independently of its parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation should refer back to a complete government in which each individual is a subject; this provides the centre of unity absent in schemes where the assembly is sole sovereign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design institutions so elected representatives are embedded within and accountable to an overarching government framework, not isolated as independent ambassadors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid undue concentration of power in a single city (capital dominance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive preëminence of a compact, powerful city (Paris) will dominate weaker, disjointed provinces and maintain control by force of numbers and organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance urban and provincial influence; provide mechanisms preventing a single urban center from monopolizing legislative and executive command.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect indirect restraints and class structures as mitigation against despotism
rubrics_metrics.description: Well-ordered classifications and indirect restraints in society (as in ancient republican design) act as barriers against excesses of despotism and give permanence to liberty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design checks and balances that may include differentiated estates, peerage, or other institutions that prevent arbitrary concentration of power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rules that frustrate learning and continuity in public office (e.g., long ineligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules disqualifying recently serving members (making every legislator ineligible for two years) prevent experience and continuity, producing governors who are 'superficial' and 'broken' in memory and practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow for the acquisition and retention of governing experience; avoid arbitrary prohibitions that remove effective practitioners from service just as they learn their trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide workable mechanisms for calling representatives to account
rubrics_metrics.description: If representatives are too far removed by electoral gradations or systemic design, primary electors cannot call them to account; responsibility must be practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure institutional means exist for constituents to hold officials responsible, and design electoral rules so accountability is meaningful and enforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable constituents to know candidates' fitness and retain influence over them
rubrics_metrics.description: Elections must permit electorates to judge the fitness of candidates and to retain some hold on them through personal obligation or dependence; purely mechanical or distant selection denies this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure nomination and election so that electors can make informed choices and maintain leverage over officials between cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit absolute sovereign power of the Assembly; provide fundamental laws and rules of proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: An assembly with every possible power and no external control, without fundamental laws or respected rules of proceeding, is unstable and likely to overreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define constitutional constraints, procedures, and maxims that bind legislatures; avoid leaving state action to the caprice of a single assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject treating the nation as a conquered territory (respect ancient boundaries and attachments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies modeled on conquerors—destroying territorial limits and past combinations—disregard the attachments that make citizens loyal and cohesive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect historic provinces, jurisdictions, and the principled attachments people have to local and ecclesiastical institutions when redesigning constitutional structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize local governments in compact, rounded bodies aligned with elective principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Local governments (departments, communes, cantons) should be compact and, where possible, composed similarly to elective assemblies so they function coherently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build local institutions that are internally consistent and capable of operating as effective elements of the larger state, rather than arbitrary fragments.
